evidence_test: cd referee && python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_sentinel.py'  # Green.test_later_runs_not_read_after_green, ThreeOfThree.test_no_runs_rerun, ThreeOfThree.test_fifth_run_not_read, ThreeOfThree.test_judged_runs_are_checked, ThreeOfThree.test_zero_test_first_run_then_passing_reruns_is_flaky, ThreeOfThree.test_no_result_in_any_judged_run_is_red, Shapes.*, CommandLine.test_unusable_exit_2. 29j flaky leaves these open; my choices, each bound by a test: (a) 'sonrakiler okunmaz' and 'ilk dordu degerlendirilir' are read as 'not read at all': a run after a green first run, or after the fourth, is neither judged nor checked for shape, so a malformed one there is not exit 2. (b) An empty runs list is 'rerun' (no first run, so not green; fewer than four), not unusable. (c) Shapes are exact: stdin only {runs}, a run only {results} with a list, a result only {id, status}, id a non-empty string, status exactly pass or fail (no skip), an id at most once per run (even with the same status); anything else is exit 2 with {verdict: null, red: [], flaky: [], revert: false}. (d) A zero-test first run whose three reruns pass is 'flaky' with flaky [] (literal reading of 'red bos degilse (ya da hicbir kosunun sonucu yoksa) red, degilse flaky'); a reader may expect a zero-test head to stay red: if so, 29j should say 'a run with zero results counts as failing' and the rule changes in one place (decide). (e) Not in the seed: who turns a contained run's output into {results: [{id, status}]} (the same gap as seed-023 for the run record), and which tests are affected beyond stage 0's whole service-free set; gate.sentinel.watch takes the rerun as a callable, which is where run.contained is called (calls 3 -> 12), so 3 -> 12 is an injection, not an import. Draft for 29j: '(a) okunmayan kosu bicim icin de denetlenmez; (b) bos runs rerun; (c) bicimler tam, fazladan anahtar ya da yinelenen kimlik kullanilamaz girdi; (d) sifir testli ilk kosu ve gecen uc yeniden kosu flaky, red bos.' and for 26a sentinel.run: name the producer of per-test results from a koş output.
